Each pin hashes a file's BODY — the whole file when body_from is null, else from the first line reading exactly body_from through EOF — so a header comment above a vendored docstring can be corrected without moving the bytes a consumer pins. A deliberate change is `python tools/vendor_sync_check.py --print`, paste the new hash, and say why in `note`. Written 2026-09-12 under G2-vendor-pins-forge.

pins.body_from: """friction_floor.py — a smoke detector for the mirror, not a wall.
pins.note: LOCAL OVERRIDE, decided 2026-09-12: this pins THIS copy's own body, not willow-gate's. Measured that day, the two are not byte-identical — this copy spells `re.I` where willow-gate spells `re.IGNORECASE` (six sites) and `typing.List`/`Optional` where willow-gate uses `list[...]`/`X | None` — a spelling-only divergence with identical behaviour (the file's own header, corrected on #25, says exactly this). willow-gate's whole-file sha256 that day: 31d4df2d9a4e2556a583c055ad6d0c8a42b3cea599920e9d38e675601bc67b99. willow-mcp pins this same body hash as EXPECTED_BODY_SHA256 in its tests/test_stance_friction.py, so editing the body here breaks willow-mcp at Forge's next release; re-syncing to willow-gate's spelling is deferred to a bite that lands both sides in the same hour. Until then a drift here means someone edited the scorer in Forge alone, which is the thing this pin exists to catch.

Canonical home. The fleet's published convention set, saved verbatim from willow-reconciler 0.6.0's CLI (trailing newline included) under G2-conventions-forge, 2026-09-12. tests/test_fleet_conventions.py reads its rules and pins the same hash naming the same version; this entry is the manifest's copy of that pin so one checker names every vendored body. A re-save from a newer reconciler is a deliberate update: run `reconciler conventions --json > tests/fleet_conventions.json`, then `--print` here, then update both this hash and DOCUMENT_SHA256/DOCUMENT_SOURCE in the test together. The document's own `sources` say what each rule was learned from; read them before changing the tree to satisfy a rule.
